concepts.name: Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule: purpose, declaration, criteria and commissions
concepts.description: Article 244, the Fifth Schedule, who declares a scheduled area and on what criteria, the ten states, the commissions and the related articles.
concepts.idea: The Fifth Schedule lets the President declare and alter scheduled areas, in consultation with the Governor, to protect tribal autonomy and the scheduled tribes.
concepts.rule: Article 244 in Part X envisages a special system for 'scheduled areas' and 'tribal areas'. The Fifth Schedule deals with scheduled areas and scheduled tribes in any state except Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram; at present ten states have scheduled areas (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan). The President may declare a scheduled area, increase or decrease it, alter its boundaries, rescind the designation or make fresh orders, in consultation with the Governor; the criteria (preponderance of tribal population, compactness and reasonable size, a viable administrative entity, economic backwardness compared with neighbouring areas) are not spelt out in the Constitution but are well established. The President must appoint a commission on scheduled areas and scheduled tribes compulsorily after ten years of commencement (Dhebar 1960, report 1961; Bhuria 2002, report 2004). Article 244A concerns an autonomous state in Assam and Article 339 Union control over scheduled areas (pp.594-595, 597).

concepts.name: Executive power, Tribes Advisory Council and Governor's regulations in scheduled areas
concepts.description: The state and Union executive roles in scheduled areas, the Tribes Advisory Council, and the Governor's power to exempt Acts and make regulations.
concepts.idea: In scheduled areas the state executes, the Centre directs, a Tribes Advisory Council advises and the Governor's regulations, with the President's assent, can override Acts.
concepts.rule: The executive power of a state extends to its scheduled areas; the Governor has a special responsibility and reports to the President annually or whenever required, and the Centre can give directions to the states. Each state with scheduled areas establishes a Tribes Advisory Council of 20 members (according to the chapter), three-fourths being representatives of the scheduled tribes in the state legislative assembly; the President may direct a similar council in a state with scheduled tribes but no scheduled areas. The Governor may direct that an Act of Parliament or of the state legislature does not apply to a scheduled area or applies with modifications. After consulting the council the Governor may make regulations for peace and good government that prohibit or restrict land transfer by or among scheduled tribe members, regulate land allotment to them and regulate money-lending, and may repeal or amend Acts; all such regulations need the President's assent (pp.594-595).
concepts.example: Regulation restricting land transfer by or among tribals.

concepts.description: Tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, their constitution as autonomous districts and regions, the councils' composition and the ten areas of Table 42.1.
concepts.idea: The Sixth Schedule makes the tribal areas of four north-eastern states autonomous districts, with a Governor who organises them and councils that govern them.
concepts.rule: The Sixth Schedule contains special provisions for the tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, framed to preserve democratic traditions and cultural diversity and conceived as tribal self-rule. The tribal areas are constituted as autonomous districts but do not fall outside the executive authority of the state. The Governor can organise and re-organise the districts (areas, names, boundaries) and divide a district with different tribes into autonomous regions. According to the chapter, a district council has 30 members, four nominated by the Governor and the rest elected on adult franchise; elected members hold office for five years unless dissolved earlier and nominated members during the Governor's pleasure; each region has a separate regional council. The Governor may appoint a commission and dissolve a council on its recommendation. Table 42.1 lists ten tribal areas: Assam 3, Meghalaya 3, Tripura 1, Mizoram 3 (pp.595-597).

concepts.name: Powers of district and regional councils
concepts.description: Law-making, judicial, executive and fiscal powers of the councils and the application of Acts to autonomous areas.
concepts.idea: Councils of autonomous areas make laws on listed matters with the Governor's assent, run village courts and local services, and raise land revenue and specified taxes.
concepts.rule: The district and regional councils administer their areas and make laws on specified matters such as land, forests, canal water, shifting cultivation, village administration, inheritance of property, marriage and divorce and social customs, all with the Governor's assent. They can constitute village councils or courts for suits and cases between the tribes and hear appeals; the Governor specifies the High Court's jurisdiction. The district council can establish, construct or manage primary schools, dispensaries, markets, ferries, fisheries and roads, and make regulations (with the Governor's assent) for the control of money lending and trading by non-tribals. The councils assess and collect land revenue and impose certain specified taxes. Acts of Parliament and of the state legislature do not apply to autonomous areas or apply with modifications; in Assam the Governor directs for both, in Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram the President for Parliament's Acts and the Governor for the state legislature's (p.596, footnote p.597).

concepts.name: Fifth versus Sixth Schedule: a comparison
concepts.description: How scheduled areas and tribal areas differ in coverage, declaration, bodies, assent, emphasis and numbers.
concepts.idea: The Fifth Schedule protects tribals through the President, Governor and an advisory council; the Sixth builds tribal self-rule through elected district and regional councils.
concepts.rule: The Fifth Schedule covers scheduled areas and scheduled tribes in all states except the four north-eastern states, which fall under the Sixth Schedule. In the Fifth, the President declares the area, a Tribes Advisory Council advises, the Governor reports to the President and makes regulations needing the President's assent; in the Sixth, the Governor organises autonomous districts, district and regional councils make laws needing the Governor's assent, and the emphasis is on self-rule because many communities had ruled themselves until the British subjugated them in the 19th century. The state's executive power extends to scheduled areas and autonomous districts do not fall outside it. Both systems allow Acts to be made inapplicable or modified. Numbers: ten states with scheduled areas, ten tribal areas, 20 members of the Tribes Advisory Council, 30 members of a district council (pp.594-597).
concepts.example: Money-lending: Fifth regulates in relation to tribes; Sixth by non-tribals.
